Religious literacy culture plays an important role in developing students’ reading habits, religious understanding, and character within the madrasah environment. This study aims to analyze the implementation of religious literacy culture, its implications for students’ reading interest, and the factors supporting and inhibiting its implementation at MTs Negeri 3 Mojokerto. This study employed a qualitative approach with a case-study design. Data were collected through participant observation, in-depth interviews with the principal, literacy coordinator, librarian, subject teachers, homeroom teachers, and students, as well as document analysis. The data were analyzed through data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing and verification. The findings show that religious literacy culture was implemented through three stages: habituation, development, and classroom learning. The main programs included Friday Literacy, morning Qur’an recitation, 10–15 minutes of reading, library visits, written summaries in literacy journals, and religious activities. These practices familiarized students with the Qur’an and religious books, strengthened their character, increased their participation in literacy activities and library use, encouraged writing, and reduced excessive mobile-phone use. The supporting factors included school leadership, teacher and parental support, the library, prayer room, reading corners, school media, religious activities, and literacy competitions. The inhibiting factors included weak intrinsic motivation, social-media and peer influence, poorly maintained reading corners, and limited use of Islamic digital media. This study concludes that a consistently implemented religious literacy culture, supported by school stakeholders and adequate literacy facilities, can strengthen students’ reading interest, religious character, and active participation in literacy activities.

topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Digital healthcare increasingly uses artificial intelligence (AI), cloud computing, and adaptive systems for predictive, personalized, continuous care. These systems face uncertainty from incomplete observations, heterogeneous data, changing patient states, and variable treatment responses. This chapter synthesizes literature on stochastic adaptive healthcare and cloud-enabled AI from technological, ethical, legal, and regulatory perspectives. It examines Bayesian updating, MDPs/POMDPs, uncertainty quantification, and queueing networks as foundations for adaptive clinical decision-making. It distinguishes aleatory and epistemic uncertainty and shows how probabilistic outputs affect trust, accountability, bias, consent, and regulation. The chapter proposes the Cloud-Based Adaptive Healthcare Governance and Implementation Framework (CAHGIF 2.0–Stochastic), integrating stochastic reasoning, organizational readiness, governance, and health outcomes. Responsible adaptive healthcare requires AI and measurement, communication, monitoring, and governance of uncertainty across AI lifecycle.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: This article reviews scientific approaches to mathematical modeling and artificial intelligence-based optimization of hydraulic regimes in urban water distribution networks. It considers uneven pressure distribution, hydraulic losses, water leakage, and energy consumption. Traditional hydraulic models, evolutionary optimization, machine learning, and digital twins are compared. The review proposes a conceptual hybrid framework combining physics-based simulation, sensor data, demand forecasting, and multi-objective optimization. The framework is presented as a research direction rather than an experimentally validated solution

Existing safety benchmarks rely largely on synthetic prompts with loosely grounded taxonomies and offer little focused analysis of severe crime categories. We introduce GUISE, a benchmark of criminal-assistance scenarios sourced from real-world cases and organised under a taxonomy from the UNODC International Classification of Crime for Statistical Purposes (ICCS). Each scenario is rendered under three linguistic framings and evaluated across five distinct cultures. Using our proposed two-tier evaluation framework, which judges both harmfulness and operational uplift, we find that: (i) framing alone drives unsafe compliance, with the mean unsafe compliance rate rising from 28.9% under direct requests to 66.4% under correction seeking (peaking at 97.3%; p < 0.05), as models correcting deliberately distorted details supply executable criminal steps; (ii) culturally adapted prompts elicit significantly more unsafe compliance than literal translations of the same requests in all four non-English languages (+7 to +18 points), a risk that translation-based benchmarks miss; and (iii) unsafe responses from the least-safe models carry strong Anglocentric registers, and the extent of this leakage increases monotonically with response harmfulness ($ρ$ = 0.46 to 0.63 across languages, all p < 0.001). GUISE offers a grounded resource and fine-grained diagnostics for strengthening refusal alignment across languages and cultures. We publish our code and data to facilitate future research.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can reason over both structured measurements and free-text records, which makes them attractive for emergency department (ED) prediction. However, most existing LLMs still fall short of conventional ML methods like trees on EHR-based prediction tasks. Our controlled analysis traces this gap to two weaknesses: LLMs do not select informative features, and they misjudge what numerical values imply for risk even when given the right features. We propose TIR-EC, a tool-integrated reinforcement learning framework that addresses both. TIR-EC exposes EHR feature groups as tools the LLM can call. It trains the LLM with rewards from a gradient-boosted tree teacher, which provides a reference set of informative tools and a graded risk target. TIR-EC also distills task-specific clinical skills into the model weights through a reverse curriculum that gradually removes the skills from the prompt during RL process. Evaluation on three clinical prediction tasks shows that our 4B agent achieves the highest macro F1 of all compared models, outperforms conventional ML baselines, and is competitive with much larger frontier LLMs. Further analysis shows that TIR-EC selects more useful evidence with fewer tool calls and combines measurements more effectively.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Machine learning models for tabular prediction typically assume that training data are representative of the population on which they will be deployed. In practice, however, data are often collected based on convenience, availability, or cost, resulting in systematic sampling biases that can distort feature--target relationships and undermine real-world generalization. Existing tabular distribution-shift benchmarks primarily construct out-of-distribution (OOD) settings by partitioning observations across naturally occurring domains. While such partitions may induce changes in P(Y | X), the resulting shifts are neither explicitly controlled nor isolated, and the evaluation distributions themselves are often not representative of the broader target population. We introduce INCONVENIENT, a benchmark designed to study robustness to convenience-sample bias. Rather than relying on naturally occurring domain partitions, INCONVENIENT directly perturbs feature--target relationships in the training distribution while preserving the original population distribution as the deployment environment. This setting more closely reflects real-world scenarios in which models are developed from unrepresentative samples and subsequently deployed on a broader population. The distinction is particularly relevant for large language models (LLMs), whose pretraining may encode population-level knowledge that extends beyond the relationships observed in a biased training dataset. Unlike existing distribution-shift benchmarks, INCONVENIENT provides explicit control over both the direction and severity of relationship shifts, enabling a systematic assessment of robustness to convenience sampling. The benchmark comprises 200 tabular classification and regression datasets spanning diverse application domains and generates around 15,500 shifted training distributions which lead to substantial downstream degradation.

LLM-powered agents increasingly support open-ended activities, yet orchestrating when and how agents interact with humans remains challenging. Existing approaches often provide interaction mechanisms tied to particular tasks or execution patterns, lacking a unified architecture for diverse and evolving interaction needs. We introduce Inflak, a unified four-layer architecture for human-agent interaction orchestration that separates state reconstruction and routing, interaction and execution planning, interaction design, and interface rendering. Its layered design with progressive resolution enables general applicability, runtime flexibility, module composability, and orchestration maintainability. We implement Inflak as agent-native, skill-based plugins within a general-purpose agent framework and evaluate it through a gallery of various application scenarios and interaction paradigms, technical performance testing, and a comparative implementation case study. The evaluations show that Inflak can serve as a general and extensible foundation for orchestrating diverse human-agent interaction flows.

Purpose This conceptual article examines wicked problems as information problems that have the potential to (1) contribute to information avoidance and (2) produce uncomfortable knowledge. It aims to bridge a gap in information science by integrating these three constructs to explain polarized individual and institutional responses, using the example of generative AI (GenAI). Design/methodology/approach Drawing on interdisciplinary literature from planning, social science and human information behavior, the study develops a unifying macro–meso–micro framework. GenAI is used as an illustrative case to demonstrate how wicked problem characteristics generate uncertainty, which in turn has the potential to trigger avoidance behaviors across levels and produce uncomfortable knowledge. Findings At the micro level, individuals avoid information as an adaptive response to affective discomfort and uncertainty. At the meso level, institutions respond through strategies such as denial, dismissal, diversion and displacement. Using the example of GenAI, these dynamics reinforce polarized, all-or-nothing responses, despite its inherent complexity. Research limitations/implications As a conceptual study, the framework requires empirical testing across contexts to validate relationships among levels. Originality/value This article offers a novel conceptual integration of wicked problems, information avoidance and uncomfortable knowledge within a single framework. It advances understanding of information avoidance as a strategic, multi-level response to complex information environments.

Artificial intelligence is reshaping teaching, learning, assessment, and professional judgment across P–16 education. This chapter presents a competency-based microcredential framework designed to prepare teacher candidates for responsible AI use before clinical practice. The framework positions AI literacy as a professional competency grounded in instructional design, ethical stewardship, data privacy, equitable access, human–AI collaboration, and reflective judgment. It moves from foundational understanding to applied classroom implementation through modules focused on responsible AI adoption, AI fluency, prompt literacy, AI limitations and risks, instructional design in AI-rich environments, classroom guardrails, and a culminating AI Integrity Statement. Drawing on literature synthesis, stakeholder feedback, policy analysis, and professional standards, including TPACK and UDL-informed approaches, the chapter offers an adaptable framework for guiding responsible implementation across educator preparation contexts.

The instrumentations, devices, and machines used in biomedical applications have a highly intricate structure that necessitates not just a substantial number of components (i.e., medical imaging machines; medical sensing devices; robotics; wearable devices; and e-Health remote monitoring systems), but also different types of technologies (mechanical, hydraulic, and pneumatic devices to operate, and electrical and/or electronic devices to control). This intricacy makes them susceptible to breakdowns and malfunctions, which can result in injuries and, in severe cases, fatal accidents. Therefore, developing effective health condition monitoring (HCM) methods is essential for handling fault detection and diagnosis (FDD), fault-tolerant control (FTC), lifecycle estimation (LCE), and prognosis and health management (PHM) in the field of biomedical engineering. This paper aims to provide a comprehensive review of the contemporary techniques for fault detection, diagnosis, and prognosis in the diversified smart-biomedical systems (SBSs) and their different applications. Ultimately, the goal is to provide a state-of-the-art platform for researchers, doctors (i.e., the operators), maintenance teams, and experts to investigate, innovate, and implement the most effective HCM techniques for their use, thereby facilitating the rapid advancement of monitoring and fault detection in biomedical engineering during a period of heightened interest in condition-based maintenance (CBM) and the incorporation of advanced technology in the medical field, particularly, with the availability of big data and the Internet of Things (IoT) within the blooming era of artificial intelligence(AI), especially at present, with the fourth industrial revolution.

This study explores the impact of integrating Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) into a flipped classroom in higher education. Using a quantitative approach with complementary qualitative data, the research involved 136 management students, yielding 77 valid responses. Data were analysed via IBM SPSS 29.0, employing descriptive, inferential, and Exploratory Factorial Analysis. Findings indicate that GenAI integration enhances student engagement and promotes a deeper understanding of AI tools. Students reported increased awareness of GenAI's capabilities and limitations, and improved critical evaluation skills. Class size emerged as a significant factor influencing participation and organizational effectiveness. Overall, results provide empirical evidence of the educational benefits of GenAI in flipped settings, supporting teaching and learning. The study contributes to discussions on fostering critical GenAI use and offers practical implications for AI-driven pedagogical strategies.

Saudi Arabia’s industrial expansion under Vision 2030 increases the strategic importance of preventing loss of containment across oil and gas, petrochemical, water, utilities, and infrastructure assets. This review examines how health, safety, and environment (HSE) governance can be integrated with intelligent leakage detection so that sensing technologies become part of accountable risk management rather than isolated technical tools. An integrative review of peer-reviewed literature published during 2020–2025 synthesizes evidence on acoustic sensing, pressure and flow analytics, Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT), machine and deep learning, digital twins, risk-based inspection, dynamic risk analysis, human factors, and safety governance. The synthesis shows that intelligent systems can improve detection speed, localization, and predictive integrity assessment, but technical accuracy alone does not ensure safer outcomes. Governance quality determines whether alerts are validated, escalated, translated into barrier actions, documented, and learned from. The paper proposes an HSE-integrated architecture linking sensor assurance, contextual analytics, dynamic risk ranking, human authorization, emergency response, maintenance, and sustainability metrics. It argues that Saudi industrial operators should treat leakage intelligence as a safety-critical decision system with defined ownership, cybersecurity controls, model assurance, and lifecycle verification. Research priorities include Saudi field datasets, explainable and uncertainty-aware models, cross-asset interoperability, human–AI decision protocols, and evidence connecting intelligent detection to measurable reductions in environmental releases and major-accident risk.

Habitat suitability assessment and conservation gap identification are critical for endangered species conservation. Using Przewalski's gazelle ( Procapra przewalskii ), an endangered ungulate endemic to China, we assessed habitat suitability, key environmental predictors, and conservation gaps in the Qinghai Lake region. Based on 1597 field occurrence records collected from 2020 to 2025, we integrated the Maximum Entropy (MaxEnt) model with explainable artificial intelligence (XAI), including SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and Partial Dependence Plots (PDPs), and GAP analysis. The selected MaxEnt model showed high discriminatory ability within the surveyed region (mean test AUC = 0.972 ± 0.003). The Human Influence Index (HII), mean temperature and precipitation of the driest quarter, elevation, and vegetation type were key predictors associated with habitat suitability, while mean diurnal range and HII had the highest mean SHAP importance. Suitable habitats were concentrated around Qinghai Lake and in the northern Gonghe Basin. The Qinghai Lake Basin represented the current core distribution area, whereas the Gonghe Basin contained extensive currently predicted suitable habitat and may represent an important conservation opportunity. GAP analysis showed that 71.83% of suitable habitat and 52.34% of the current distribution range lay outside the protected-area boundaries assessed in this study. Fence occurrence in the Hubei population area was significantly associated with relatively high predicted habitat suitability and showed marked spatial clustering. These findings provide spatially explicit evidence for protected-area optimization and habitat management of Przewalski's gazelle.

Understanding wave phenomena requires students to integrate physical representations, quantitative relationships, and scientific reasoning. This study investigated the integration of PhET simulations and ChatGPT within the 7E Learning Cycle to support high school students’ conceptual understanding of waves. A quasi-experimental pretest–posttest design involved 71 Grade XI students, comprising 35 students in the experimental group and 36 in the control group. The experimental group received integrated 7E–PhET–ChatGPT instruction, while the control group received Direct Instruction. Conceptual understanding was assessed using ten validated essay items covering five conceptual-reasoning indicators and three higher-order cognitive dimensions. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics and baseline-adjusted regression with HC3 robust standard errors. The experimental group demonstrated higher adjusted posttest performance, with a difference of 12.18 percentage points (95% CI [6.76, 17.60]). The largest differences occurred in quantitative application (38.76 points) and scientific reasoning and investigation (30.06 points). Written responses illustrated more explicit conceptual differentiation, quantitative justification, evidence evaluation, and independent investigation design. These findings suggest that integrating simulations and AI-supported clarification within structured learning activities is associated with stronger conceptual reasoning, although classroom-level confounding and the short intervention limit causal interpretation.

This article analyzed scientific evidence on the application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) to HIV prevention, diagnosis, and care, emphasizing ethical challenges and perspectives for Brazilian nursing. An integrative literature review was conducted using PubMed/MEDLINE, SciELO, the Virtual Health Library/LILACS, and DOI tracking mechanisms, including publications from 2015 to August 2026 in Portuguese, English, or Spanish. Twenty-five studies with verifiable DOI were selected, covering machine-learning applications for risk stratification and pre-exposure prophylaxis indication, automated interpretation of rapid tests, prediction of adherence, disengagement and viral suppression, counseling support, and algorithmic equity. Findings showed that AI can broaden the identification of priority populations, support clinical decisions, improve diagnostic interpretation, and enable personalized interventions during therapeutic follow-up. However, data bias, model opacity, privacy, stigma, information security, and technological dependence require governance, local validation, and professional oversight. It was concluded that Brazilian nursing can play a strategic role in the responsible implementation of these technologies by combining clinical judgment, health education, data protection, and person-centered care.
